title: Halting from an Answer State
statement: Let $C,e\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{mode}$ and $b$ be Boolean values, let $f$ map finite Boolean strings to finite Boolean strings, let $h$ be a finite Boolean string, and let $B\in\mathbb{N}$. For any vector $v$ of fourteen natural-number registers whose entries are at most $B$, the computation started in the answer state for $b$, with register vector $v$ and no result yet, halts with result $b$. Every configuration strictly before halting satisfies the machine precondition and has all registers at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps finite Boolean strings to finite Boolean strings
$v$ is a vector of fourteen natural-number registers
Every register of $v$ is at most $B$
replaced:
For all natural numbers $C,e$, Boolean values $\mathrm{mode},b$, every function $f$ on
finite bit strings, every input bit string $h$, every bound $B\in\mathbb N$, and every
vector $v$ of fourteen natural-number registers whose entries are at most $B$, the
specified machine started in its answer state for $b$, with registers $v$ and no answer
yet, halts with answer $b$. Every configuration before halting satisfies the machine's
precondition and register bound.
